source: Mock — modeled on the publicly documented splunk/botsv3 ("Frothly") CTF storyline, not parsed from downloaded data
note: Synthetic demo chain, kept in the same shape as datasets/Security-Datasets/apt29-attack-chain.json so Citadel has a second scenario to render.

steps.description: Employee (Kevin) opens a malicious attachment, dropping an initial payload.
Payload executes a malicious PowerShell/VBS script on the laptop.
AWS access keys found stored in plaintext files/browser data on the compromised laptop.
Stolen AWS credentials used to authenticate to the victim's AWS account from an external IP.
Attacker enumerates EC2 instances, S3 buckets, and IAM users/policies.
New/existing EC2 instances repurposed to run cryptomining software.
Sensitive files pulled from an exposed/compromised S3 bucket.
Collected data exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
Legitimate IAM users locked out / credentials rotated by the attacker to hinder response.
